synopsis.synopsisDesc: The Office of Insular Affairs (OIA) is requesting funding proposals for its Brown Treesnake (BTS) Control Program to prevent the migration of the BTS from Guam to other United States jurisdictions; to suppress and control the BTS on Guam to support the restoration of the island's native ecosystems; to avoid electrical outages to civilian or military facilities caused by the snakes; and to ultimately develop the capability to eradicate the BTS from Guam.The Administration will prioritize projects that drive economic growth, ensure reliable and affordable energy, and strengthen national security and regional stability.
synopsis.responseDateDesc: Electronically submitted applications must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m., ET, on the listed application due date (deadline has been extended to June 8, 2026).
synopsis.fundingActivityCategoryDesc: Brown Treesnake (BTS) program funds are provided to prevent the migration of the BTS from Guam to other United States jurisdictions; to suppress and control the BTS on Guam to support the restoration of the island's native ecosystems; to avoid electrical outages to civilian or military facilities caused by the snakes; and to ultimately develop the capability to eradicate the BTS from Guam.
synopsis.applicantEligibilityDesc: Eligible applicants are limited to members and active participants of the Brown Treesnake Technical Working Group which includes, but is not limited to, representatives of the governments of Guam, the Commonwealth Northern Mariana Islands, and Federal Agencies, in accordance with 2 CFR 200.
synopsis.modComments:
The deadline for the Office of Insular Affairs" Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs) has been extended to June 8, 2026. This extension is being offered in recognition of the significant impacts caused by Super Typhoon Sinlaku, which has affected applicants" ability to prepare and submit materials on the original timeline.
 
We hope this additional time will help ensure that all eligible entities are able to fully participate in the application process.
